question: What are the guidelines for disaster-related procurement?
expected_answer: GPPB Resolution No. 17-2026 (approved 14 August 2026) approves the Guidelines on Procurement for Disaster-Related Preparations and Response, issued as Circular No. 08-2026 (Annex A). The Guidelines govern procurement for disaster preparedness, anticipatory measures, and disaster-related mitigation, response, relief, recovery, rehabilitation and reconstruction during a State of Calamity (RA 10121) or a State of Imminent Disaster (RA 12287), applying the fit-for-purpose approach of RA 12009 balanced with proportionality and transparency. The Resolution also amends Section 35.2 (Negotiated Procurement – Emergency Cases) and Section 100.1 of the IRR of RA 12009, and directs the GPPB-TSO to monitor and review the Guidelines.
notes: Circular No. 08-2026

question: What documents are required for eligibility in negotiated procurement according to the TSO?
expected_answer: In the opinion of the GPPB-TSO (NPM No. 025-2026, 16 September 2026), the eligibility documents for negotiated procurement are only those expressly prescribed for the specific mode and ABC under Section 4 of GPPB Resolution No. 10-2026 / Circular No. 06-2026, which Section 3.5 makes exclusive. The PhilGEPS registration requirement may be met with either the PhilGEPS Organization ID (Red Membership) or the Certificate of Registration (Platinum Membership) under Section 4.3.1. An ITR, AFS, Tax Clearance, PCAB License or other document kept in PhilGEPS for Platinum Membership should not be required just to verify PhilGEPS registration; it is required only if that procurement mode prescribes it, and need not be re-submitted if the PE already holds an updated copy (Section 4.4). The TSO notes this is not the official position of the GPPB.
